name: pearcinema
description: Your self-hosted film and TV collection, playable anywhere. P2P video player with no port forwarding, no VPN and no account.

scripts.verify: node --test --test-concurrency=4 test/*.test.js && npm run build:dashboard && npm run build:ui

//test-concurrency: FOUR WORKERS, NOT ONE PER CORE, and it is the difference between 14 seconds and
a run that looks hung. node --test defaults to os.availableParallelism(), which
is 12 here - and these are not ordinary unit tests. Several files spawn REAL
ffmpeg processes and REAL 3-node HyperDHT testnets, so twelve workers is twelve
times that, several times oversubscribed, and the DHT ones are timing-sensitive
enough that they simply stop making progress.
It presents as a HANG rather than a failure: every test that ran passes, the
last files scheduled never report, and the reflex is to raise a timeout rather
than look. Diagnosed 2026-08-13 after it swallowed several runs.
//: THE HOST HAS ITS OWN DEPENDENCY SET and it is deliberately small, because
almost everything it does is inherited from @peerloom/host: the HyperDHT
server, the firewall, pairing, the grant store, revoke and the media channel.
@peerloom/host is consumed as a file: dependency, matching how @peerloom/core
and @peerloom/device-link already work. It runs in NODE ON A SERVER, not in a
Bare worklet on a phone, so core's native-addon `overrides` block does NOT
apply and must not be copied here.
//main: expo-router's entry. The host is `npm run host` - it never cared about main.
